question.text: During DD on Chambal Opportunities Fund, the LP team asks about 'competing or outside interests' of the Investment Manager. Per Ch 12, which of the following is a legitimate LP concern?

answer.text: The Manager's employees taking paid vacation.
The Manager's use of external printing vendors for marketing collateral.
The Manager's payment of GST on management fees.

Other AIF interests, business obligations or outside ventures of the IM that compromise time devoted to the fund, external professional engagements where fees are charged to the fund, and board positions in investee companies that may create disclosure conflicts.

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12 explicitly covers: referral of deals if Manager runs multiple funds, time-allocation, outside business interests, professional-service fees charged to fund, and nominee-director conflicts in investee companies. The Trap: A, B, C are operational minutiae, not competing interests. Cross-Exam Context: Same conflict-of-interest taxonomy as XXI-B (PM — outside interests disclosure) and X-A (IA — conflict disclosures). Manager's Pro-Tip: Publish an 'Outside Interests Register' updated quarterly — shows all key persons' board seats, advisory roles, other AIF mandates. LPs appreciate proactive disclosure more than defensive denial.
